title: The zero-differential normal form of a periodic tensor
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $t=(t_U)_U$ a restriction-compatible family of sections with $t_U^2=0$. Let $M$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] such that multiplication by $t$ on $M$ is zero. Define a cochain complex $P$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] by $P^i=\mathcal O$ for $i\leq0$, $P^i=0$ for $i>0$, and differential multiplication by $t$ for $i<0$, zero otherwise. Let $Z_M^i=M$ for $i\leq0$ and $Z_M^i=0$ for $i>0$, with every differential zero, and let $M[0]$ have $M$ only in degree zero. There is an isomorphism of cochain complexes $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}M[0])\cong Z_M$ for the total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Its degree-$i$ map for $i\leq0$ is induced by the unit tensor isomorphism $\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathcal O}M\to M$, locally $a\otimes m\mapsto am$, with inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. These isomorphisms are natural in $\mathcal O$-linear maps of sheaves annihilated by $t$, and $H^{-q}(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}M[0]))\cong M$ for every $q\geq0$, while its positive cohomology vanishes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In particular, if $\varepsilon:P\to E[0]$ is a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex] of an $\mathcal O$-module sheaf $E$, this zero-differential complex represents the tensor $E[0]\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}M[0]$ computed using that resolution. This assertion includes ordinary modules by taking the one-point site; no annihilator condition on $\mathcal O$ and no nonzero hypothesis on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: The examples: the all-degree Tor computation after tensoring the periodic resolution; generalized to an arbitrary annihilated module sheaf

proof.text: For $i<-1$, the composite $d_P^{i+1}d_P^i$ is multiplication by $t^2=0$. At $i=-1$ or $i\geq0$ one of the two differentials is zero. The scalar maps are restriction-compatible and $\mathcal O$-linear by commutativity. Thus $P$ is a cochain complex. The displayed $Z_M$ and $M[0]$ are complexes because their differentials are zero.

source.place: Section 010V (section-complexes), cochain-complex definition; direct verification for the periodic complex

proof.text: For every object $U$, the balanced map $u_U:\mathcal O(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}M(U)\to M(U)$ sends $a\otimes m$ to $am$, and $v_U(m)=1\otimes m$. The equations $u_Uv_U(m)=m$ and $v_Uu_U(a\otimes m)=1\otimes am=a\otimes m$ prove that they are inverse module maps. Both commute with restriction since restrictions respect multiplication and $1$. By the universal property of module sheafification, they induce inverse maps $\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathcal O}M\rightleftarrows M$: the composites are identities since this holds before sheafification. This constructs the unit isomorphism without assuming tensor sections are already a sheaf. The same argument shows $0\otimes M=M\otimes0=0$, since the presheaf tensor is zero on every object.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product) and Lemma 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), explicit unit maps

proof.text: Put $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{\mathcal O}M[0])$. Its degree-$n$ coproduct has only one possibly nonzero summand: $P^n\otimes M$ at $(p,q)=(n,0)$. Indeed all other summands contain the zero term of $M[0]$. Projection to this summand, zero on the others, is inverse to its coproduct injection: check each composite on every injection. Thus $T^n\cong P^n\otimes M$, with no infinite-product or boundedness assertion needed. For $n\leq0$ compose this projection with the unit map of step 2 to obtain $\phi^n:T^n\to M$; its inverse is the injection after $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. For $n>0$ both $T^n$ and $Z_M^n$ are zero. These give degreewise inverse graded maps $\phi:T\rightleftarrows Z_M:\psi$.

The second contribution $(-1)^p(1\otimes d_{M[0]})$ to the total differential is zero in every bidegree. For $n<0$ the first contribution sends a local tensor $a\otimes m$ to $(t_Ua)\otimes m$; under the unit maps this becomes $t_Uam=a(t_Um)=0$, by the hypothesis on $M$. Since pure tensors generate the presheaf tensors and the maps extend uniquely to their sheafifications, this is equality of sheaf morphisms. For $n=0$ the target is zero, and for $n>0$ the source is zero. Hence every differential of $T$ becomes zero under $\phi$. Both $\phi$ and its degreewise inverse $\psi$ commute with differentials, and their composites are identities in every degree. They are inverse cochain-complex isomorphisms.

source.place: The examples: the periodic Tor calculation, expanded as the signed differential and sheafification computation

proof.text: Let $f:M\to N$ be an $\mathcal O$-linear morphism between sheaves killed by $t$. The induced total map has the sole nonzero summand $1\otimes f$ in degree $n\leq0$. On a local pure tensor the two composites in the naturality square are $a\otimes m\mapsto af(m)$ and $a\otimes m\mapsto f(am)$; they agree by linearity. The inverse square is $1\otimes f(m)=(1\otimes f)(1\otimes m)$. Uniqueness of sheafification extension proves these equations for sheaf maps, and all positive-degree squares are between zero objects. Thus the isomorphisms are natural in the claimed maps.

source.place: The examples: naturality of the generalized tensor calculation, checked on pure tensors

proof.text: For a zero-differential complex, $\ker d^n$ is the entire term and $\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}=0$, so $H^n(Z_M)=Z_M^n/0\cong Z_M^n$. Apply the functor $H^n$ to the complex isomorphism just constructed. This gives $H^{-q}(T)\cong M$ for all $q\geq0$ (including $q=0$), and $H^n(T)=0$ for $n>0$. On the one-point site the same tensor and sheaf maps are ordinary module maps. The formulas also apply when $t=0$, $M=0$, or the ring sheaf is zero; no nonvanishing or annihilator equality was used.

source.place: The examples: all nonnegative Tor degrees, including degree zero; elementary kernel/image computation

proof.text: Now suppose $\varepsilon:P\to E[0]$ is a K-flat resolution. By its definition $P$ is K-flat and $\varepsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the ringed-site comparison $c_{P,M}$ of [lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison], which requires neither termwise flatness nor boundedness of $P$ nor flatness of $M$. It identifies $Q(P)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}Q(M[0])$ with $Q(T_M(P))$, where $T_M(P)^n=P^n\otimes M$ and its differential is $d_P^n\otimes1$. Steps 3–4 identify this termwise tensor complex with $Z_M$. Since localization makes $Q(\varepsilon)$ invertible, tensoring its inverse with $1$ identifies $Q(E[0])\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}Q(M[0])$ with $Q(P)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}Q(M[0])$. Their composite is the asserted representation by $Z_M$, computed from the specified resolution.
